narrative.overview:
ReviveCheck sells on-chain release approvals as permissions a contract enforces, and the site is built like a commercial infrastructure product: a marketing landing that opens into a live dashboard. The ground is cool paper, never white; everything that carries content is a white card on a 1px hairline, so the page reads as a desk of records rather than a document. The hero does not describe the product, it shows the recorded approval: a card with the approval block as a large rolling numeral, a transaction-status card whose steps check off on load, and a "Listing allowed" toast overlapping its corner, all over a faint masked grid and two soft Portaldot glows. The app keeps the same desk at operating restraint: a 60px bar, a sidebar, cards, tiles, and the live finalized head rolling in the overview's hero card.

Color is scarce and means something. One indigo does the action and the live number: the primary pill button, links and chain references, the counters in the stats band, the current nav item, the "App" tag. Three status triads (green pass, red fail, amber hold) appear as a dot and a soft tint, or as status-colored text, never as a block. One near-black band holds what is enforced: the rules band on the landing, the lifecycle tab panel, the "Run it with your own wallet" card, and the dark readback panels. The Portaldot violet-to-azure gradient is the co-brand and the live signal: hero glows, the contract dots in the sidebar, the running stage's border, the current transaction pill, the indeterminate sweep, and the closing band.

Motion is one fast-out settle ease applied sparingly: blocks rise 14px as they enter, every chain number rolls in as an odometer, the hero's status steps fire in sequence, the lifecycle tabber advances under a linear progress rule, and mega-menus scale-fade in. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` every animation and transition is removed and the finished state is rendered at once. The world is light only (`color-scheme: light`, `theme-color #f5f6f8`); selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring and the native select chevron are themed to match.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground with white hairline cards; near-black ink and four grays; two hairline weights.
Geist on its weight axis for every text role (650 display, 600 titles, 550 UI, 400 body); Geist Mono with tabular figures only for chain data and code.
Indigo pill buttons (40/32/48px) with a soft indigo glow; white hairline pills as the secondary.
Status is a dot plus a soft tint; the running state breathes.
One dark band for the rules; the Portaldot gradient only as glows, co-brand and live progress, plus the closing band.
Every chain number is a rolling odometer; cards rise 14px on entry; nothing moves under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Paper-And-Card Rule
rules.body: The page ground is cool paper and content lives on white hairline cards. A white page ground, or a card drawn directly on another card without a hairline, breaks the desk.

rules.name: The Indigo-Leads Rule
rules.body: Indigo means the action or the live number: the one primary button in a view, links and chain references, counters, the current item, the running state. Its washes mark "current" or "product" and nothing else; indigo never fills a heading, a card body or a status.

rules.name: The One-Dark-Band Rule
rules.body: Near-black surfaces hold what is enforced or recorded: the rules band, the lifecycle panel, the wallet card and the readback panel. There is no dark theme and no dark section outside these.

rules.name: The Gradient-Is-Live Rule
rules.body: The Portaldot gradient reads as soft glows behind the hero and the app's hero card, as the co-brand dot, on live progress (the running stage, the current transaction pill, the sweep), and as the closing band. A static card, heading or button never carries it.

rules.name: The Dot-And-Tint Rule
rules.body: Status is a 6px dot plus a soft tint badge with a matching line, or status-colored text. No status ever fills a solid block.

rules.name: The Chain-In-Mono Rule
rules.body: Every hash, address, block link, runtime version, command and code sample is Geist Mono with tabular figures. Headline numerals (the approval block, the live head, the counters) are Geist, not mono: the number is the headline, its link is the chain reference. Prose, labels and headings are never mono.

rules.name: The Tighter-As-Larger Rule
rules.body: Tracking tightens with size: −0.045em at display and numerals, −0.04em at headline and stats, −0.035em at page titles, −0.03em at titles, −0.015em at small titles, −0.005em on buttons, zero on labels, captions and mono.

rules.name: The Number-Is-The-Headline Rule
rules.body: A recorded block number is set as the largest type on its card, with a caption above it and a chain link beside or below it; a block number never appears only as small mono.

rules.name: The Card-Not-Band Rule
rules.body: Rhythm comes from cards on the paper ground and hairlines, not from alternating page bands. The only full-width tints are the stats band (paper subtle) and the closing band (gradient); the dark band is a card inside the column.

rules.name: The Raised-Means-Evidence-Or-Overlay Rule
rules.body: The raised shadow belongs to the hero's recorded cards, product visuals, and anything that overlays the page (mega-menus, dialogs, toasts). Working cards and tiles stay on the hairline shadow; hover may lift a stage node one step and 1px.

rules.name: The Radius Ladder Rule
rules.body: Controls are pills; fields 8px; tracks and sidebar links 10px; code, tables and nodes 12px; cards 16px; the hero's recorded cards 18px; the dark panel 20px; the dark band 24px. Pick the step by what the element is; do not invent intermediate radii.

dos: Do keep the ground cool paper and every content surface a white card on a 1px hairline; use the four text grays (ink, ink-2, ink-3, ink-4) and the three hairlines (line, line-strong, line-hover) for every neutral need.

Do set every hash, address, block link, runtime version, command and code sample in Geist Mono with tabular figures, link chain values to the official explorer in indigo, and set a card's headline block number as a large Geist numeral that rolls in as an odometer.
Do express status as a dot plus a soft tint badge (pass, fail, hold, run, quiet), a kind chip, or status-colored text.

Do use pills for every button and chip, 8px for fields, 10px for tracks and sidebar links, 12px for code and nodes, 16px for cards, 18px for the hero's recorded cards, 20px for the dark panel and 24px for the dark band.
Do keep the raised shadow for the hero's recorded cards, product visuals, mega-menus, dialogs and toasts; working cards and tiles sit on the hairline shadow.

Do put the Portaldot gradient only on glows, the co-brand dot, live progress and the closing band, and show the official Portaldot mark unaltered, only as "Built on … Portaldot V3", with clear space of at least a quarter of its height.

Do focus with the 2px indigo outline at a 2px offset (white on the band and the gradient; inputs take an indigo border plus a 16% ring), and remove every animation and transition under `prefers-reduced-motion` while rendering the finished state.
donts: Don't set the page ground white, place a card on a card without a hairline, or alternate page-wide bands; the stats band and the closing band are the only full-width tints.
Don't fill a heading, a card body or a status with indigo, or use its wash for anything but "current" and "product"; one indigo primary per view.
Don't fill status as a solid block; a badge is a soft tint with a line and a dot.
Don't add a dark theme or a dark section beyond the rules band, the lifecycle panel, the wallet card and the readback panel (`color-scheme: light`).
Don't apply the Portaldot gradient to a static card, a heading or a button, and don't recolor, outline, crop or animate the Portaldot mark or imply endorsement.
Don't introduce a third face, uppercase tracking-out labels or kickers, a display weight above 650, a hard offset shadow, or a second easing beyond the settle ease and the odometer's roll.
Don't let an entry stagger exceed 300ms or an odometer roll longer than 1.1s, and don't animate anything that has not finished loading its real value.
